title: Place Value to 100,000: Expanded Notation and Composing Numbers
seo_title: Grade 3 Place Value to 100,000 Worksheets: Expanded Notation (TEKS 3.2A, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.2A compose and decompose numbers up to 100,000 as a sum of so many ten thousands, so many thousands, so many hundreds, so many tens, and so many ones using objects, pictorial models, and numbers, including expanded notation as appropriate; 3.2B describe the mathematical relationships found in the base-10 place value system through the hundred thousands place
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 place value worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.2A and 3.2B: read and write numbers to 100,000, the value of a digit, expanded form and expanded notation, composing numbers in different ways and the 10 times relationship. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: A digit's value is the digit times its place.
key_sub: Each place is 10 times the place to its right. 14 thousands is the same as 1 ten thousand and 4 thousands.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each digit has a place: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. Its value is the digit times its place.
  • Each place is 10 times the place to its right. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand; 10 thousands make 1 ten thousand.
  • Expanded form adds the values: 40,000 + 5,000 + 200 + 6. Expanded notation shows the multiplication: (4 × 10,000) + (5 × 1,000) + (2 × 100) + (6 × 1).
  • A number can be made in more than one way: 45,206 is also 3 ten thousands, 15 thousands, 2 hundreds and 6 ones.

Examples

Example

Write 30,405 in expanded form.

3 ten thousands = 30,000

0 thousands: skip

4 hundreds = 400

0 tens: skip

5 ones = 5

Answer: 30,000 + 400 + 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying the digit, not its valueMultiply by the place: the 5 in 45,206 is worth 5,000.
Leaving out a zero: 40,050 written as 4,050Use 0 to hold every empty place.
Thinking a place can only hold 0 to 9 when you decompose14 thousands is fine. It is 1 ten thousand and 4 thousands.

faq.q: What does TEKS 3.2A ask Grade 3 students to do?
faq.a: Compose and decompose numbers up to 100,000 as so many ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, with pictures, numbers and expanded notation.

faq.q: What is the difference between expanded form and expanded notation?
faq.a: Expanded form adds the value of each digit (40,000 + 5,000 + 6). Expanded notation shows each digit times its place value ((4 × 10,000) + (5 × 1,000) + (6 × 1)).
Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. The 3 in 3,000 is worth 10 times the 3 in 300 (TEKS 3.2B).

faq.q: How is place value tested on the STAAR?
faq.a: Questions ask for the value of a digit, which number matches a model or expanded notation, and another way to make a number, such as 15 thousands instead of 1 ten thousand and 5 thousands.
